Child: (focused on the tablet, looking at the screen)

Child: "The Grinch hadn-" (looking at the screen, attempting to read)
Parent: (quietly watching, hand supporting chin)
Child: "Hated." (sounding out the word)
Parent: (nods slightly, still looking at the child)
Child: "It couldn't be his... Oh my God... It couldn't be his head wasn’t scre-" (continuing to read, glancing at the parent)

Parent: (same position, still watching the child)
Child: "On just right. It could be, perf-" (pauses slightly, then continues)
Parent: (closely observing, hand on chin)
Child: "Per-haps" (reading the word slowly and carefully)
Parent: (nods slightly, encouraging)
Child: "Perhaps that his shoes were too tight. But I think that the most likely reason of all may have been that his heart was two sizes too small." (completes the sentence with more confidence)
Parent: (smiling, looking pleased)
Child: (sitting at the table, looking at the tablet)
Parent: "But whatever the reason his heart or his shoes, he stood there on Christmas Eve heating the Who's."
Child: (continues to look at the tablet)
Parent: "He- not 'heating'... Ha-"
Child: (still looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Hating."
Child: (turns head to look at the parent)
Parent: "Hating, yes."
Child: (looks back at the tablet)
Parent: "That's what I said."
Child: (looks at parent)
Parent: "You said 'heating'."
Child: (still looking at parent)
Parent: "No, I said 'hating'."
Child: (still looking at parent)
Parent: "Okay. Do it again, 'hating'."
Child: (looking at parent)
Parent: "Hating.... Oh my God. Hating the Whos."
Child: (looking at the tablet, reading) "Staring down from his cave with a sour Grinchy frown..."

Child: (still looking at the tablet) "Be-neath."
Parent: (pointing at the word on the tablet) "Beneath."
Child: (looking at the tablet and continues reading)
Parent: (watching child) "I helped you."

Parent: "Was busy now heading..."

Child: (looking at the tablet)

Child: "And they... their socks... socking-"

Child: "Dad stop touching the book."

Child: (reading more confidently) "Dad! Stockings, he snarled with a sneer. Tomorrow is Christmas, it's practically here. Prac-tally here."

Parent: "Pra-cti-cally. Pra-cti-cally."

Parent: "Then he growled with his Grinch fingers nev-er-y drumming. Then he growled with his Grinchy fingers never drumming. I must find some way to stop Christmas from coming. For tomorrow, he knew, all the Who girls and boys would wake bright up and early. They rush for their toys. And then, oh, the noise. Oh, the noise, noise, noise, noise, noise. The one thing he hated, the noise, noise, noise, noise, noise."
Child: (focused on the tablet, looking at the screen)
Parent: "Then the Whos... young and old, sit down to a feast. And they feast, feast, and they feast and they feast and feast, feast, feast. They would feast on Who pudding and rare Who roast beast."

Parent: "Which... something the Grinch couldn't stand in the least. And then they do something he liked least of all. Every Who down in Whovillage, tall and small... Small... Would stand close together, with Christmas bells ringing. They'd stand hand in hand and the Whos would start singing."

And the more the Grinch thought of this Who Christmas sing, the more the Grinch thought, I must stop this whole thing. The more the Grinch thought, I must stop this whole thing... Stop this whole thing."

Parent: "Why for fifty-three years I've put up with this now. I must stop this Christmas from coming, but how? Then he got an idea. An awful idea. The Grinch got a wonderful, awful idea."
Child: (looks curious, remains focused)
Child: (sitting at the table holding the tablet, looking at the screen)
Parent: "I know just what to do. The Grinch laughed in his throat. And he make a quick Santy Claus hat and a coat."

Parent: "Did that stop the old Grinch? No. The Grinch... Simply said if I can't find a reindeer, I'll make one instead. So he took his dog Max, and he took some re- thread. And he tried a big horn on the top of his head."

Child: (leaning back with a smile)
Parent: "Then?"
Child: (looking at the tablet, hands resting on the table)
Parent: "Then he loaded some bags and some old empty stacks on a ramply sled..."

Child: (listening attentively to the story)

Parent: (sitting beside the child, looking at the tablet) Then he slithered and slunk with a smile most unpleasant, around the whole room and he took every present. Pop guns and bicycles, roller skates, rusk-rusky drums, check boards, [inaudible 00:13:29] and plums.

Parent: (maintains focus on the tablet) Can I correct this? Tricycles.
Child: (still looking at the tablet) Tricycles. And he stuffed them all in bags. Then he Grinch, very numbly, stuffed all the bag, one by one, up the chimney.

Child: (continues reading from the tablet) Then he slunked to the icebox, he took the Whos' feast. He took the Who pudding. He took the roast beast. He cleaned out that icebox as quick as a flash. He... Why that Grinch even took the last can of Who hash. What's Who hash? Who hash?

Parent: Are they eating wormies there? A can of wormies?

Child: (Continues looking at the tablet)
Parent: (Nods slightly, watching the child) Okay.

Child: (Looks back at the tablet, turning the page)
Parent: Oh, who is coming back?

Child: (Points at the tablet and reads aloud) And the Grinch grabbed the tree, and he started to shove, when he heard a small sound, like the coo of a dove. He turned around fast, and he saw a small Who. Little Candy-Who-
Parent: (Corrects the child gently) Cindy. Not candy. Cindy.

Child: (Reads from the tablet again) Who who was not more than two. The Grinch had been caught by this tiny who daughter who got out of bed for a cup of cold water. She started at the Grinch and said Santa Claus, why, why, why are you taking our Christmas tree? Why?

Child: (holding the tablet and reading aloud) "But you know, that old Grinch was so smart and so slick, he thought up a lie and he thought up it quick. I'll fix it up, then I'll bring it back here."

Child: (focused on the tablet, reading) "And his flub- his flub-"

Child: (correcting himself) "Fib... The children, then he patted her on her head and he got her a drink... went to... and sent her to bed. And then Cindy-Lou Who went to bed with her cup, he went to the chimney and stuffed the tree up."
Parent: (nodding, listening closely)
Child: (continuing to read intently) "Then he last thing he took was a log for the fire. Then he went up the chimney and [inaudible 00:18:13]. On the walls he left nothing but hooks and some wire."

Child: (engaged and looking at the tablet, following along with the reading)

Parent: (leans on hand, listening and watching the child closely)
Child: (still engaged, eyes focused on the tablet)
Parent: " [foreign language] Then he did- did the same thing to the other Whos' house- to the Whos' house... Who houses... Leaving crumbs much too small for the other Who mouses."
Child: (remains focused on the screen, continues to follow along)
Parent: (leans back slightly, watching the child interact with the tablet)
Child: (looking at the tablet, reading along)

Parent: "It was a quarter past dawn, all the Whos still in a-bed. All the Whos still a-snooze when he packed it up his sled. Packing it up with their presents, their ribbons, their wrappings. Packed up- packed it up with their presents and ribbons and wrappings. Their tags and tinsels and their tringings and their tappings?"

Parent: "Another page? Is there another page? Oh."
Child: (continues reading, focused) "That noise, grinned the Grinch, that I simply must hear. So he passed-"

Child: (corrects and continues) "And the Grinch put his hand on his ear. And he did hear a sound rising over the snow. It started in low, then it started to grow. But the sound wasn't sad. Why this sound merry. I couldn't be so. But it was merry very. He started down at Whovillage, the Grinch popped his eyes. Then he shook what he saw was a shocking surprise."
Child: (looking at the tablet, seeming focused on the storybook)
Parent: (leaning in, watching the child and listening to the story)
Child: "Every who down in Whovillage, the tall and the small, was singing without a present at all."

Child: (turning a page on the tablet)

Child: "He hadn't stopped Christmas from coming. It came. So how or other it came just the same. And the Grinch, with grinchy feet ice cold in the snow, stood puzzling and puzzling how could it be so? It came without ribbons, it came without tags. It came without packings, boxes, or bags. Then he puzzled three hours 'till he puzzle was sore. Then the Grinch thought of something he hadn't before. Maybe Christmas, he thought, doesn't come from a store- from a store. Maybe Christmas, perhaps, means a little bit more."

Parent: "Need help?"
